title: Estimation of Pregnancy Rate in the Wild Population of Caspian Seals (Pusa caspica, Gmelin, 1788)
content:
ABSTRACT

The Caspian seal population has an “Endangered” conservation status on the IUCN Red List, and it is necessary to obtain up-to-date data on pregnancy rates using minimally invasive methods. In November 2022 and 2023, live Caspian seals were captured in the Kazakh waters of the North Caspian Sea, from which blood and hair samples were collected, and ultrasound diagnosis was performed. In 2022, hair samples from dead individuals found on the coast were collected, and necropsies were performed to determine pregnancy. Adult females had higher plasma progesterone concentrations than young females, but age category had no significant effect on hair progesterone concentration. The threshold to identify pregnant females was a plasma progesterone concentration of > 105.2 ng/mL. Using this threshold, pregnancy rates were 60% in 2022 and 54% in 2023. Females identified as pregnant using this method had higher body mass and girth than non-pregnant adult females (body weight: W = 71, p < 0.02; girth: W = 76.5, p < 0.04, Mann–Whitney test). Necropsies of dead individuals revealed fetuses in 36 of 42 females, with a pregnancy rate of 86%.
